newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reed Elsevier buys Chilton, expands in U.S. publishing.
newsitem.headline: Reed Elsevier buys Chilton, expands in U.S. publishing.

text.p: Reed Elsevier, announcing its third U.S. acquisition this year, said Monday it would spend $447 million to buy trade magazine publisher Chilton Business Group from Walt Disney Co.
The Anglo-Dutch publishing group, which earlier this year acquired 40 U.S. legal publications from Thomson Corp., said the deal would make an immediate contribution to its profits.
Chilton, which publishes 39 business magazines, focusing on manufacturing, entertainment and automotive topics, made a pre-tax profit of $28 million in 1996 on sales of $203 million.
Since 1992, the company, which is based in Radnor, Pa., has achieved compound pre-tax profit growth of 17 percent.
Reed-Elsevier said it would merge Chilton's core trade press business with its own U.S. business magazines unit, Cahners Publishing Co, which has a stable of more than 90 titles.

Group strategy director Peter van Hooff said that by combining Chilton and Cahners, Reed-Elsevier could raise its U.S. business publishing operating profit margins to around 20 percent in 1999 from some 15 to 17 percent now.
Van Hooff said the deal would significantly strengthen Reed Elsevier's U.S. trade magazine publishing business, providing plenty of scope to raise revenues and cut costs.
Reed Elsevier would also be able to write off 80 percent to 90 percent of the purchase price against U.S. taxes over 15 years.
Van Hooff said Reed-Elsevier would eliminate overlap between previously competing titles and make them more complementary.
"The combination of Cahners and Chilton gives us even stronger positions in more markets," he said.

Chilton's magazines will also broaden and deepen the editorial content that Reed-Elsevier is able to offer via electronic media, he said, noting that Chilton did not previously have its own electronic publishing infrastructure.
"The Chilton titles will really benefit from the lead we have in electronic publishing," he said.

Van Hooff said Reed-Elsevier, which owns leading U.S. show business newspaper Variety, had already been planning an online information service for the entertainment industry and that the Chilton deal would add further momentum to this project.
Analysts generally welcomed the Chilton buy, saying it was a good fit with Cahners but not a major strategic move.
"This is a nice build-on acquisition, it can be integrated nicely and has obvious tax advantages," said Jeff Meys of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Chilton's science publishing division bought MDL Information Systems Inc. for $320 million this year.
